title: Vector Fields Flows and Lie Derivatives

items.title: A smooth vector field is a smooth section of the tangent bundle
Smoothness of a vector field is equivalent to smooth coordinate components
items.strategy: In an induced tangent-bundle chart, a section has the form p -> (x(p), X^1(p), ..., X^n(p)). The tangent-bundle section is smooth exactly when those coefficient functions are smooth, and the change-of-coordinate formula shows that this criterion is chart-independent.

items.title: The action of a vector field on smooth functions
A vector field acts as a derivation of smooth functions
items.strategy: Apply the pointwise Leibniz rule in each tangent space T_pM. The resulting function is smooth because in local coordinates it is the sum of the smooth coefficients X^i times the smooth partial derivatives of the target function.

items.title: Derivations of smooth functions are exactly smooth vector fields
items.strategy: For each point p, the values D(f)(p) define a tangent derivation at p, hence a tangent vector. In coordinates, the coefficient functions are D(x^i), so they are smooth, and uniqueness follows because tangent vectors are determined by their action on smooth functions.

items.title: F-related vector fields
F-relatedness is equivalent to the derivation intertwining law
items.strategy: Unpack dF_p(X_p)=Y_{F(p)} against a test function f on the target. Evaluating both sides on f gives X(f o F)=(Yf) o F, and conversely agreement on all smooth functions determines the tangent vectors at each point.

items.title: Pushforwards and pullbacks of vector fields by a diffeomorphism
A vector field along an embedded submanifold extends to a neighbourhood and globally when the submanifold is closed
items.strategy: In slice charts, extend the tangential and normal coefficient functions off the slice and glue those local extensions with a partition of unity on a neighbourhood of the submanifold. If the submanifold is closed, a smooth cutoff equal to 1 near it and supported in a tubular neighbourhood turns that neighbourhood extension into a global one.

items.title: A vector field tangent to an embedded submanifold restricts to a vector field on it
items.strategy: In a slice chart for the submanifold, tangency forces the normal coordinate components of the ambient field to vanish on the slice. The remaining tangential components restrict to smooth functions on the slice, so they define the induced field on the embedded submanifold.

items.title: The Lie bracket of smooth vector fields
The commutator of vector-field derivations is again a derivation
items.strategy: Expand X(Y(fg)) and Y(X(fg)) using the Leibniz rule twice. The second-order terms agree and cancel after subtraction, leaving exactly the first-order Leibniz expression for a derivation.

items.title: Coordinate formula for the Lie bracket
items.strategy: Write X=X^i d/dx^i and Y=Y^i d/dx^i in a chart and apply the commutator to each coordinate function x^j. The mixed second-derivative terms cancel, leaving the coefficient formula X^i del_i Y^j - Y^i del_i X^j.

items.title: Smooth vector fields form a Lie algebra under the Lie bracket
items.strategy: Bilinearity, antisymmetry, and the Jacobi identity are the corresponding identities for operator commutators on C^infty(M). The previous lemma and derivation-to-field reconstruction ensure that the commutator stays inside the smooth vector fields.

items.title: Leibniz rules for the Lie bracket with function multiples
items.strategy: Expand [X,fY](g) and [fX,gY](h) directly from the commutator definition and use the derivation property of X and Y. The derivative correction terms are exactly the obstruction to C^infty-bilinearity.

items.title: Related vector fields have related Lie brackets
items.strategy: Test the bracket against an arbitrary smooth function on the target and use the intertwining law twice. The two commutator expressions match term by term, so the resulting brackets are F-related.

items.title: Diffeomorphism pushforward preserves Lie brackets
items.strategy: A diffeomorphism carries every vector field to an F-related one, so the previous proposition applies with F and F^{-1}.

items.title: Coordinate vector fields commute
items.strategy: In a coordinate chart, the coefficient functions of d/dx^i and d/dx^j are constant. The coordinate formula therefore gives zero for every coefficient of their bracket.

items.title: Integral curves of a vector field
Local existence, uniqueness, and smooth dependence for manifold integral curves
items.strategy: Choose a chart near the initial point and transport the field to a smooth Euclidean vector field. The Euclidean local-flow theorem gives a local solution depending smoothly on the initial point, and uniqueness forces chart solutions to agree on overlaps.

items.title: Through each point there is a unique maximal integral curve
items.strategy: Any two integral curves through the same point agree on the overlap of their domains by local uniqueness. The union of all such overlap-compatible curves is again an integral curve, and the union of their interval domains is an interval, giving the maximal one.

items.title: Complete vector fields
Local and global flows generated by a vector field
The fundamental theorem on flows
items.strategy: Let D be the union of the domains of the maximal integral curves and define Phi(t,p) to be the point reached by the maximal curve through p at time t. Local smoothness comes from the manifold local-flow theorem, openness of D follows by transporting a local flow along each maximal curve, and the local group law follows from uniqueness after a time shift.

items.title: Time-t flow maps are diffeomorphisms between open domains
items.strategy: On the maximal flow domain, the local group law gives Phi_t o Phi_-t = id and Phi_-t o Phi_t = id on the relevant time slices. Thus Phi_t is a diffeomorphism with inverse Phi_-t between the two open fibre domains.

items.title: The generating vector field is invariant under its own flow
items.strategy: Fix t and push forward the integral curve of X through p by Phi_t. The pushed-forward curve solves the same X-equation as the integral curve through Phi_t(p), so uniqueness forces (Phi_t)_*X = X on the common domain.

items.title: A vector field is complete if and only if its flow is global
items.strategy: By definition, completeness means that every maximal curve is defined for all real times. The maximal flow is therefore defined on all of R x M exactly in that case.

items.title: Compactly supported smooth vector fields are complete
items.strategy: Outside the compact support, integral curves are stationary. If a maximal curve failed to exist for all time, its image would still lie in the compact support together with its initial point, so the standard compact-continuation argument used in the flow theorem would extend it past the finite endpoint, a contradiction.

items.title: Every smooth vector field on a compact manifold is complete
items.strategy: The support of a vector field is closed, and a closed subset of a compact manifold is compact. Thus every vector field on a compact manifold is compactly supported, so the previous theorem applies.

items.title: The flow of a vector field tangent to a closed embedded submanifold preserves it
items.strategy: A tangent field restricts to a vector field on the embedded submanifold. Starting from a point of the submanifold, both the ambient integral curve and the intrinsic one solve the same initial-value problem there, so uniqueness makes them agree wherever both are defined.

items.title: The flow-box theorem
items.strategy: At a point where X_p is nonzero, choose local coordinates with one coordinate increasing along X and take the transverse slice where that coordinate is zero. The map sending (t, slice point) to its flow image has invertible differential at the base point, so the inverse function theorem turns it into a local diffeomorphism and straightens X to d/dx^1.

items.title: A nonvanishing vector field has locally parallel integral curves
items.strategy: In flow-box coordinates, the field is d/dx^1, whose integral curves are the parallel coordinate lines with the other coordinates fixed.

items.title: The flowout of an embedded submanifold by a vector field
The flowout theorem
items.strategy: Let S be a codimension-one slice transverse to X and consider the map (t,p) -> Phi_t(p). Its differential is invertible at (0,p) because the time direction maps to X_p while the slice directions map to T_pS, which together span T_pM. The inverse function theorem gives a local embedding and uniqueness of integral curves yields injectivity after shrinking.

items.title: The Lie derivative of a function
The Lie derivative of a vector field
The Lie derivative of a vector field equals the Lie bracket
items.strategy: Apply the defining difference quotient for the Lie derivative to an arbitrary smooth function and differentiate through the pushforward expression. The inverse-time pushforward in the definition makes the sign come out as L_X Y = [X,Y], not its negative.

items.title: A vector field is flow-invariant if and only if its Lie derivative vanishes
items.strategy: The curve t -> (Phi_-t)_* Y_{Phi_t(p)} is constant exactly when its derivative at 0 vanishes. By definition that derivative is L_X Y, so vanishing is equivalent to invariance under the X-flow.

items.title: Two vector fields commute if and only if their local flows commute
items.strategy: If [X,Y]=0, the previous proposition says that Y is invariant under the X-flow, so the X-flow sends Y-integral curves to Y-integral curves and uniqueness yields commuting local flows. Conversely, differentiate the flow-commutation identity at the identity time to recover the vanishing Lie bracket.

items.title: Related complete vector fields have intertwined flows
items.strategy: For each p, the curves t -> F(Phi_t^X(p)) and t -> Phi_t^Y(F(p)) solve the same Y-integral-curve problem with the same initial condition. Completeness makes both curves global, so uniqueness gives equality for every t.

items.title: Time-dependent vector fields and their evolution operators
Time-dependent vector fields have local smooth evolution operators
items.strategy: In local coordinates, the equation becomes a nonautonomous smooth ODE. The Euclidean nonautonomous theorem gives solutions depending smoothly on the initial time and initial point, and chart uniqueness lets those local solution operators patch on manifold overlaps.

items.title: Time-dependent evolution satisfies the two-time cocycle law
items.strategy: Starting at time s, evolve first to t and then from t to r. Both the composite curve and the direct curve solve the same time-dependent initial-value problem on the overlap, so uniqueness forces equality.

items.title: Compactly supported time-dependent vector fields have global evolution on a compact time interval
items.strategy: Assume the supports of all time slices lie in one compact subset K and the time interval J is compact. A maximal solution can only move inside K or remain stationary outside it, so finite-time breakdown would again contradict the compact-continuation argument; compactness of J then lets the local evolution be continued across the whole interval.

items.title: FALSE: every pointwise assignment of a tangent vector is a smooth vector field
items.strategy: On R, the assignment x -> |x| d/dx gives a tangent vector at every point, but its coefficient function is not smooth at 0. So pointwise tangent data alone do not define a smooth vector field.

items.title: FALSE: every smooth vector field can be pushed forward by every smooth map
items.strategy: For the projection F(x,y)=x on R^2, the field X=y d/dx gives dF(X_(x,y))=y, which depends on the fibre point (x,y) and so cannot define a vector at x alone. A pushforward exists without ambiguity only under an F-relatedness or diffeomorphism hypothesis.

items.title: FALSE: every smooth vector field is complete
items.strategy: The vector field x^2 d/dx on R has integral curves x(t)=x_0/(1-x_0 t), which blow up at t=1/x_0 for x_0>0. So smoothness alone does not force global existence.

items.title: FALSE: the Lie bracket is C^infty-linear in each vector-field entry
items.strategy: The Leibniz rule [X,fY]=f[X,Y]+(Xf)Y shows the extra derivative term directly. Unless Xf vanishes identically, multiplying one entry by a function changes the bracket by more than pointwise scaling.

items.title: FALSE: the point values X_p and Y_p determine the bracket value [X,Y]_p
items.strategy: At p=0 in R, the pairs (d/dx, x d/dx) and (d/dx, 0) have the same point values, but their brackets at 0 are d/dx and 0. The bracket therefore depends on first derivatives of the coefficient functions, not only on point values.

items.title: FALSE: a vanishing Lie bracket forces the vector fields to be pointwise linearly dependent
items.strategy: The coordinate fields d/dx and d/dy on R^2 commute, but they are linearly independent at every point. So commutation is about first-order compatibility of flows, not pointwise span.

title: Vector Fields Flows and Lie Derivatives — Examples

items.title: Constant vector fields have translation flows
items.strategy: For a constant field v on R^n, solve x'(t)=v explicitly as x(t)=x_0+tv and read off the global flow Phi_t(x)=x+tv. This makes the group law and completeness completely transparent.

items.title: The radial vector field has the dilation flow
items.strategy: For X=sum x^i d/dx^i on R^n, solve x'(t)=x(t) componentwise to get x(t)=e^t x_0. The resulting flow is dilation by e^t and is defined for all times.

items.title: The planar rotation field has the circle rotation flow
items.strategy: For X=-y d/dx + x d/dy on R^2, solve the linear system x'=-y and y'=x. The solution is the standard rotation matrix, so the flow rotates each circle about the origin.

items.title: The vector field x^2 d/dx has finite-time escape
items.strategy: Solve x'=x^2 explicitly to obtain x(t)=x_0/(1-x_0 t). The denominator vanishes in finite positive time for x_0>0, so the field is incomplete.

items.title: A compactly supported cutoff of an incomplete vector field is complete
items.strategy: Multiply x^2 d/dx by a smooth bump that equals 1 near the origin and vanishes outside a compact interval. The field agrees with the incomplete model where intended, but the compact-support theorem forces the cutoff field itself to be complete.

items.title: A coordinate computation of a nonzero Lie bracket
items.strategy: Take X=d/dx and Y=x d/dx on R and apply the coordinate formula. The bracket is d/dx, so the example isolates the derivative correction term concretely.

items.title: Commuting coordinate fields have commuting flows
items.strategy: On R^2, the fields d/dx and d/dy have translation flows in the x- and y-directions. Those translations commute directly, illustrating the bracket-zero criterion for commuting flows.

items.title: Two pairs of vector fields can agree at a point and still have different bracket values there
items.strategy: At 0 in R, compare (X,Y)=(d/dx, x d/dx) with (X',Y')=(d/dx,0). The point values agree, but the brackets are d/dx and 0 at the origin, so equal point data do not determine the bracket.

items.title: A time-dependent translation field and its evolution operator
items.strategy: For X_t=a(t) d/dx on R, integrate x'(t)=a(t) to get Psi_t,s(x)=x+int_s^t a(r)dr. The formula shows explicitly why a time-dependent evolution operator depends on both start and end times.

items.title: Flow-box coordinates for a nonconstant planar field
items.strategy: For X=d/dx+y d/dy on R^2, use the coordinates u=x and v=ye^{-x}. Then X(u)=1 and X(v)=0, so in (u,v)-coordinates the field becomes d/du and its integral curves are straight parallel lines.
